newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota to introduce stock options in 98/99 -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to introduce stock options in 98/99 -- paper.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp plans to introduce a stock option system for its employees, a Japanese business daily said on Wednesday.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said Toyota was likely to give the right to buy several thousand Toyota shares a year to senior executives initially. The scheme may be introduced in the financial year from next April 1, it said.
Companies are expected to be allowed to offer stock options to their employees in the current fiscal year, it said.
Toyota was not immediately available for comment on the report.
A stock option system enables employees to buy shares in their company at specified prices as an incentive.
A panel of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party and its allies will urge the government to allow all companies to introduce employee stock options in 1997/98, party sources said last week.
Stock options are popular in the United States and Europe but are only allowed at venture capital companies in Japan under the nation's commercial code.
